keyVerseText: For verily I say unto you, Till heaven and earth pass, one jot or one tittle shall in no wise pass from the law, till all be fulfilled.
rootMeaning: The Greek verb παρέρχομαι (parérchomai) is derived from the preposition παρά (para), meaning 'beside' or 'near,' combined with ἔρχομαι (erchomai), meaning 'to come' or 'to go.' Literally, it conveys the sense of coming alongside or passing by something or someone. This etymology enriches the common English glosses such as 'pass' or 'pass away' by emphasizing movement in proximity or alongside, suggesting not just transit but a relational or spatial closeness in the action.
usageInScripture: In Scripture, παρέρχομαι appears 31 times with a range of translations including 'pass away,' 'pass,' 'past,' and occasionally 'let' or 'will come forth.' Most frequently it denotes the passing away of time or events, highlighting the transient nature of earthly realities. It also describes physical movement, such as people or ships passing by, and metaphorically can indicate the passing away or neglect of something. This variety in usage shows the word's flexibility in expressing both literal and figurative passing, underscoring temporal and spatial transitions.
theologicalSignificance: Understanding παρέρχομαι deepens our grasp of God's unchanging nature amid the passing of time and circumstances. The word's emphasis on passing by or passing away highlights the temporary nature of the created order in contrast to the enduring Word of God. This aligns with the biblical theme that while heaven and earth may pass away, God's law and promises remain steadfast. The verb also invites believers to consider what it means to pass through life faithfully, not neglecting God's commands. Ultimately, it points to Christ's eternal presence and the fulfillment of God's redemptive plan that transcends temporal passing.
keyVerseReflection: In Matthew 5:18, Jesus declares that 'till heaven and earth pass, one jot or one tittle shall in no wise pass from the law, till all be fulfilled.' The use of παρέρχομαι here emphasizes the certainty and permanence of God's law despite the inevitable passing away of the physical cosmos. This verb powerfully contrasts the temporal nature of creation with the enduring authority of Scripture, assuring believers that God's word will not fail or disappear but will be fully accomplished.
